quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: You want to turn at an intersection but you are in the wrong lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and make your turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less effectively.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
When you drive slower, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less effectively.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires can remove water from the surface. At high speeds, your tires may lose grip entirely and hydroplane, which means your vehicle slides on a layer of water.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way stop intersection. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before crossing.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors several times a minute to spot tailgaters or cars passing. If a car follows too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
Can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive so poorly that they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they look drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to road hazards.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A bicycle repair shop is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest way to drive is to:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: You must stop and back up right away.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, watch for shaded areas under trees or buildings. These spots freeze faster than other roads and are the last places to dry.

questions.question: You reach a blocked intersection. You should:

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a crossbuck sign. You should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for an approaching train.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is okay.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Obey any flagger at the crossing.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line down the center of a road means neither direction of traffic can cross it to pass.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign show?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols show construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Do not cross railroad tracks unless your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Use caution when approaching them. On a hill with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and be ready to stop. Look and listen for trains in both directions on all tracks before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the tracks and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic signals control traffic and prevent crashes. Follow them unless a police officer is directing traffic. When an officer is present, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: What should you do if you see angry drivers around you?
questions.explanation: When drivers are angry, keep your distance from them. Avoid eye contact and don't make hand gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can safely do to stay away from danger.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights at an intersection are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers like you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: You cannot leave a child under age eight alone in a vehicle if it is unsafe.
questions.explanation: Never leave a child under age eight alone in a vehicle if it could harm them. A person at least 12 years old must always watch the child.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the vehicle catches you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then pull over.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what is your first step?

options.text: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: Find a parking space, check traffic, and signal. Then stop parallel to the car in front of your space before turning your wheel to park.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to share half a lane.
Share the same lane when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same rights as other vehicles. Give the rider a full lane to move safely. Even if there seems to be enough space for two vehicles, the motorcycle needs room to stay safe.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and another person is injured, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm while you wait for help. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of the freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the shoulder of a freeway except in an emergency.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because it is unlikely another vehicle is coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may cause a crash. Never pass by driving on the highway shoulder. Do not pass by crossing a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When are U-turns not allowed?

options.text: In a curve in the road.
On a hill where you cannot see 500 feet ahead in each direction.
Near a sign that says no U-turns.

questions.explanation: In Nevada, U-turns are allowed on most roads if they are safe. They are not allowed on hills with less than 500 feet of visibility in each direction, in curves, or near no U-turn signs.

questions.question: Can drivers text while driving?

options.text: Yes, if they are very skilled drivers.
Yes, if their eyes leave the road for only a moment.

questions.explanation: You cannot use a cell phone or handheld device to talk while driving unless you use a hands-free device. You also cannot send, read, or use text messages or other non-voice communications while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with no traffic lights or stop signs?

options.text: Keep your speed and drive through.
Stop at the intersection, look in all directions, and then go.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by releasing the gas pedal, covering the brake, and checking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink if you will drive.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: How should you enter a highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. When merging, turn on your signal, find an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into the opening.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, whether there is a traffic light, crosswalk, or neither.

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. Always obey warning signs. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If you can, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: After an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

questions.explanation: You must stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle away from traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes—other vehicles could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, look:

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look at the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the bright lights—they can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: If your accelerator gets stuck while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Reach down and attempt to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Shift quickly into neutral and press the brake pedal firmly. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must bear either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means something is not allowed. Right turns are prohibited where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry about it since all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious defects to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where and how all the vehicle's controls work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where and how all the vehicle's controls work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, find the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Learn how each one works. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: It is best to keep space around your vehicle:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.
